items.name: replay-button
items.title: ReplayButton
items.description: Controlled replay icon whose arrow charges from tail to arrowhead as the host animation progresses, then unlocks.

api.summary: Ink replay button with a 44px minimum hit area. While `charging`, the circular shaft draws on over the first 85% of `progress` and the arrowhead over the last 15%; clicks are ignored and the button stays focusable with aria-disabled. When not charging it shows the complete icon and calls `onReplay` on click. No internal timer and no Remotion dependency.

props.name: progress
props.description: Normalized progress of the host animation, 0–1. Clamped; non-finite values count as 0. Ignored (treated as 1) when `charging` is false.

props.name: charging
props.description: True while the host animation plays: shows the partial charge and blocks activation (aria-disabled, still focusable). False shows the complete icon and allows replay.

props.name: onReplay
props.description: Called on click only when neither `charging` nor `disabled` is set; restart your animation here.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name (aria-label) for the button.

props.name: iconSize
props.description: Width and height of the icon in pixels; the button adds 9px padding on each side.

stage.basis: iconSize 26 plus 9px padding on each side gives 44×44, which is also the enforced minimum hit area. Size grows with iconSize (iconSize + 18); the gallery demo uses iconSize 52 for a 70×70 button.

items.name: scene-spec
items.title: SceneFromSpec
items.description: Compiles a YAML-shaped scene spec into a Remotion scene for either orientation, with timed blocks, explicit layouts, orientation overrides, and configurable safe areas.

api.summary: Renders one SceneSpec as a full-canvas Scene for one orientation. Blocks (big, stat-row, note, callout, bullets, chips, code, spacer, screens, catalog, propagate, shelf, twice, brand, overlay) stack inside the safe area with `gap` between them; `composition` and `variants[orientation]` choose the layout (flow, hero, headline-illustration, illustration), safe area, headline ratio, subject scale, and optional block overrides. Anchors resolve through `host.resolve`, text through `host.t`. It does not fit, shrink, or paginate content, and throws on invalid layouts, anchors, gaps, or insets. It does not validate the spec's shape (an unknown block type renders nothing): validate parsed YAML against the JSON Schema in `schemas` first. Every block, field, default, unit, and error is listed in the scene spec guide in `docs`.

props.name: spec
props.description: One parsed scene (SceneSpec): required id and blocks; optional anchors (needed only when a block time names an anchor), title, starts, composition, variants, gap, and valign. The compiler takes plain objects; parse YAML in the host (the guide uses js-yaml 4 `load`) and validate against #/$defs/SceneSpec of the JSON Schema.

props.description: landscape (for a 1920 × 1080 composition) or vertical (1080 × 1920); picks stage geometry, block sizes, and variants.

api.summary: Resolves a block time: a number of seconds, an anchor name, or an anchor with a signed offset such as "explain+0.2".

params.name: at

params.name: host
params.description: Supplies `resolve(phrase)` in seconds.

api.returns: Seconds from scene start. Throws on malformed, unknown, or non-finite anchors.

api.summary: Safe-area rectangle in canvas pixels for an orientation and safe-area preset or custom insets.

params.name: orientation
params.description: landscape or vertical; selects stage[orientation].

params.name: safeArea
params.description: legacy (default; portrait bottom 480), full (portrait 100/72/100/72, landscape 90/120/90/120), social (portrait 160/160/320/72), or explicit { top, right, bottom, left } insets.

api.returns: { left, top, width, height } in canvas pixels. Throws when insets are negative, non-finite, or leave no content area.

api.summary: Timing and translation services injected by the video project: `resolve(phrase)` and optional `t(s)`.
One scene: required id and blocks; optional anchors, title, starts, composition, variants, gap, valign.
The parsed YAML file: `{ scenes: SceneSpec[] }`.
Any block body plus an optional `until` exit cue.
safeArea, layout, headlineRatio, subjectScale, gap, valign, and an optional full blocks override.
"legacy" | "full" | "social" | explicit pixel insets { top, right, bottom, left }. Social applies to vertical only; in landscape it falls back to full (90/120/90/120).
`{ landscape, vertical }` pixel values, accepted wherever a size may differ per orientation (gap, spacer h, screens and propagate h).
One stat-row card: at, label, value, optional sub and valueColor.
The optional `until` cue every block accepts: fade out and drift up over 0.4 s.
The block union without `until`, discriminated by `type`.
"flow" | "hero" | "headline-illustration" | "illustration".
A time: anchor name (optionally with an offset) or seconds.

stage.basis: SceneFromSpec renders a Scene that fills its parent (position absolute, inset 0); use a 1920 × 1080 composition for landscape and 1080 × 1920 for vertical. Blocks lay out inside sceneGeometry(orientation, safeArea).

    { type: "screens", pieces: [{ kind: "card", at: "build" }, { kind: "button", at: "build+0.6" }], phoneScale: 1.5 },

props.description: Color of characters the sweep has not reached yet.

props.name: accentColor
props.description: Color of the leading wave between dim and settled characters; keep the vermilion accent.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Final color of settled characters, and of every character at progress 1.

props.name: reducedMotion
props.description: When true, renders the complete text in textColor regardless of progress.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged over the defaults (Geist sans, weight 800, line-height 1.15, pre-wrap); set fontSize here.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name on the outer span.

items.name: scroll-stack
items.title: ScrollStack
items.description: Stack any React content as you scroll. Successive items scale into place while earlier ones fade. Page or contained scrolling, keyboard access, and a plain-list fallback.

api.summary: A list region whose direct children become sticky items: each incoming item scales from 1.06 to 1 as it pins, and the item it covers shrinks toward `minScale` and fades out over the last 35% of its progress. Uses native scroll and sticky positioning (page or contained), never intercepts scroll, and scrolls a covered item back into view when keyboard focus reaches it. It falls back to a plain list under reduced motion, with fewer than two items, or when any item is taller than the viewport minus twice `top`.

props.name: children
props.description: Each direct child is one stack item; its content and styling stay yours. Keep backgrounds opaque for a solid stack; wrap related content in one element.

props.name: height
props.description: Omit to stack against page scrolling. Set a number for a self-contained, focusable scroll viewport of that many stage pixels (minimum 160; non-finite falls back to 480).

props.name: distance
props.description: Scroll distance in pixels between successive items while stacking (also the margin between them). Minimum 0; non-finite falls back to 120. The plain list uses a fixed 24px gap.

props.name: top
props.description: Sticky inset from the top of the viewport (or the contained region), in pixels; also the list's top padding. Minimum 0.

props.name: minScale

items.name: file-cabinet
items.title: FileCabinet
items.description: SVG cabinet enclosure around a controlled filing drawer whose folders slide out and lift.

api.summary: An SVG <g> for use inside your own <svg>: a fixed card enclosure with a chamfered top, and a Cajon drawer inset 10px at the sides and 32px from the top. `open` and per-folder `pulled` are controlled 0–1; the enclosure never moves or resizes.

props.name: x
props.description: Left edge of the enclosure in the parent SVG's units.

props.name: y
props.description: Top edge of the enclosure.

props.name: w
props.description: Enclosure width; the drawer is w − 20.

props.name: h
props.description: Enclosure height; the drawer is h − 44.

props.name: folders
props.description: Folders in the drawer, index 0 nearest the front. Each has a `name` (tab label, truncated after 16 characters), optional `accent` fill, and optional `pulled` 0–1 lift. Count never changes the drawer size; more than six pack closer.

props.name: open
props.description: Drawer opening from 0 (closed) to 1 (open). Clamped.

api.summary: The enclosure alone, so composites (such as Escritorio) can draw foreground furniture between it and the moving drawer.

props.name: x
props.description: Left edge in the parent SVG's units.

props.name: y
props.description: Top edge.

props.name: w
props.description: Width.

props.name: h
props.description: Height.

api.summary: Computes the enclosure box and the drawer props FileCabinet renders, for composites that draw the parts separately.

params.name: x
params.description: Left edge of the enclosure.

params.name: y
params.description: Top edge of the enclosure.

params.name: w
params.description: Enclosure width.

params.name: h
params.description: Enclosure height.

params.name: folders
params.description: Drawer folders, passed through to the drawer.

params.name: open
params.description: Drawer opening 0–1, passed through to the drawer.

api.returns: `{ body: Box, drawer: CajonProps }`: the enclosure box and the inset drawer props (x + 10, y + 32, w − 20, h − 44).

stage.basis: Default w 300 by h 360 in the parent SVG's units, placed at x, y. The drawer stays inside the enclosure at every opening, but lifted folders rise above the top by up to about their height plus 24 (roughly 190 units at the default width), so the parent viewBox needs headroom: the gallery uses "0 -260 500 700".

examples.title: Open cabinet with one folder
examples.code:
import { FileCabinet } from "@/jbm/ui/file-cabinet"

<svg viewBox="0 -260 500 650">
  <FileCabinet x={80} folders={[{ name: "datos" }]} open={1} />
</svg>

import { FileCabinet } from "@/jbm/ui/file-cabinet"

<svg viewBox="0 -260 500 700">
  <FileCabinet x={85} y={-20} w={330} h={350} open={0.8}
    folders={[{ name: "análisis", accent: true, pulled: 0.6 }, { name: "diseño" }]} />
</svg>

qa: Drag Open through 0, 0.5, and 1: the enclosure never moves or resizes and only the drawer travels toward the viewer.
Try folder counts 0, 1, 3, 6, and 12: the drawer size is unchanged and extra folders pack toward the back.
Drag Lift front folder to 1: the folder body is complete behind the drawer front, keeps its size, and stays within the viewBox headroom.
Check the preview at narrow widths; the SVG scales with its viewBox.

items.name: paper-clip
items.title: PaperClip
items.description: Independent ink wire clip to lay across a paper edge.

api.summary: Decorative (aria-hidden) wire clip: one 3px round-capped ink stroke in a 34×62 viewBox. It does not own the paper; position it over an edge yourself. All SVG attributes pass through to the root <svg>, so width, height, and style (e.g. absolute positioning) are set by the caller.

stage.basis: Default width 26 and height 48 attributes on a 34×62 viewBox. Override width and height together to scale (the gallery shows 50×92); the viewBox keeps the drawing's proportions.

examples.title: Clip across a card edge
examples.code: import { PaperClip } from "@/jbm/ui/paper-clip"

qa: Inspect the loop at default and enlarged sizes: the single stroke has round caps and even width.
Place it over a paper edge and check the part above the edge reads as clipped on, not floating.
Confirm it stays aria-hidden and adds no focusable element.

items.name: clipped-note
items.title: ClippedNote
items.description: Paper note with an optional paper clip, rotation, and paper, accent, or ink stock.

api.summary: Composes Paper (10px radius, 18px padding, 220px wide up to 100% of its container) and PaperClip. Children render in bold sans with ink matched to the stock and wrap anywhere.

props.name: children
props.description: Note content.

props.name: clip
props.description: Shows the paper clip across the top edge at left 18px, top −24px. The clip extends above the note's box.

props.name: tone
props.description: Paper stock: `paper` (card with ink text), `accent` (vermilion), or `ink`; text switches to cream on accent and ink.

props.name: rotate
props.description: Rotation of the whole note, clip included, in degrees.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged last onto the Paper, e.g. width, padding, or font size.

stage.reason: Width is 220px (maxWidth 100%) unless style overrides it; height follows the wrapped children plus 36px padding and a 4px border. The clip adds 24px above the top edge, and rotation enlarges the visual footprint.

examples.title: Rotated clipped note
examples.code:
import { ClippedNote } from "@/jbm/ui/clipped-note"

<ClippedNote clip rotate={-3}>Revisar el resultado.</ClippedNote>

examples.title: Small note attached to a paper tape
examples.code:
import { ClippedNote } from "@/jbm/ui/clipped-note"
import { PaperTape } from "@/jbm/ui/paper-tape" // install @jbm/paper-tape separately

<PaperTape length={700} window={280} attachments={[{ id: "note", at: 650,
  content: <ClippedNote style={{ width: 108, fontSize: 12, padding: 10 }}>12 de 30 rutas</ClippedNote> }]} />

qa: Toggle Paper clip: the note does not shift, and the clip overlaps the top edge rather than floating above it.
Toggle Accent paper and try ink: text stays legible on each stock.
Drag Note rotation to both extremes: the clip rotates with the note and nothing is clipped by the preview.
Check a long unbroken word wraps inside the 220px width on narrow screens.

items.name: punched-tag
items.title: PunchedTag
items.description: Card-stock luggage-style label with a punched hole and bold content, in paper, accent, or ink stock.

api.summary: A Paper with a rounded 36px left end, a 14px cream punched hole ringed in ink, and 28px extra-bold content beside it. Width follows content up to 100% of the container.

props.name: children
props.description: Tag content, usually a short name; wraps anywhere when space runs out.

props.name: tone
props.description: Stock: `paper` (card with ink text), `accent` (vermilion), or `ink`; text switches to cream on accent and ink.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged last onto the Paper, e.g. width or padding.

stage.reason: Width follows the content (14px hole + 18px gap + text) plus 40px horizontal padding and a 4px border, capped at 100% of the container. Height is one 28px line at normal line height plus 32px padding and 4px border, and grows when the text wraps.

examples.title: Ink tag
examples.code:
import { PunchedTag } from "@/jbm/ui/punched-tag"

<PunchedTag tone="ink">Modelo</PunchedTag>

qa: Toggle Ink stock: the hole stays cream with an ink ring and the text stays legible.
Check a long label at narrow width: it wraps inside the tag and the hole keeps its 14px circle.
Compare the shadow and edge with other paper surfaces.

items.name: paper-line
items.title: PaperLine
items.description: Line of text with controlled grapheme reveal, ink lift, strike-through, and dotted underline.

api.summary: Inline-block line of handwritten-on-paper text. Every progress input is controlled 0–1 (clamped; non-finite values count as 0) with no timer, so a slider or video timeline drives it. Hidden graphemes keep their space, and a visually hidden copy exposes the full text to assistive technology.

props.name: text
props.description: The line's text; revealed by whole graphemes (emoji and combined characters stay intact).

props.name: reveal
props.description: Share of graphemes shown, 0–1; visible count is ceil(reveal × graphemes). The full footprint is reserved at every value.

props.name: lift
props.description: Ink lift 0–1: the line moves up to 60px right and 40px up, rotates up to −9°, and fades (opacity 1 − lift²).

props.name: strike
props.description: Vermilion 2px strike-through across the middle, drawn left to right as 0–1 of the line width. Meant for single short lines.

props.name: dotted
props.description: Adds a 2px dotted underline in the dim color.

props.name: accent
props.description: Uses the vermilion accent for the text instead of ink.

props.name: mono
props.description: Uses the mono font stack instead of sans.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged last onto the outer span, e.g. fontSize or fontWeight (both inherit by default).

stage.reason: Inline-block text at the inherited font size with line-height 1.4; width follows the text up to 100% of the container and height grows when it wraps. Lift translates up to 60px right and 40px up without affecting layout, so leave headroom (the gallery pads 32px above).

examples.title: Partly written line
examples.code:
import { PaperLine } from "@/jbm/ui/paper-line"

<PaperLine text="Una idea clara." reveal={0.7} lift={0} strike={0} />

examples.title: Crossed-out mono note
examples.code:
import { PaperLine } from "@/jbm/ui/paper-line"

<PaperLine text="v1 descartada" mono dotted strike={1} style={{ fontSize: 22 }} />

qa: Drag Reveal from 0 to 1: graphemes appear left to right, the line never changes width, and 0 shows nothing.
Drag Lift ink to 1: the line drifts up-right, tilts, and fades out completely without overlapping controls.
Drag Strike to 1 on a single line; on a wrapped line the stroke sits at the block's vertical middle, so keep struck lines short.
Toggle Dotted underline and Accent ink independently, and check each combination with mono.

items.name: stamp
items.title: Stamp
items.description: Vermilion rubber-stamp impression that drops, makes contact, and inks in as a 0–1 press progresses.

api.summary: Bordered mono text in vermilion with a faint offset second impression. An ink impression, not a validation verdict. `press` is controlled with no timer: the stamp descends from 60px above until contact at 0.62, and its ink fades in from 0.5 to fully opaque at 0.8.

props.name: text
props.description: Impression text in 24px bold mono; wraps anywhere when space runs out.

props.name: press
props.description: Press progress 0–1 (clamped). Invisible below 0.5, touches down at 0.62, fully inked from 0.8.

props.name: angle
props.description: Rotation of the impression in degrees; negative tilts counter-clockwise.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged last onto the outer element. Setting transform or opacity here replaces the press animation.

stage.reason: Inline-block sized by the text: one 24px mono line plus 8px/16px padding and a 3px border, up to 100% of the container. Before contact it sits up to 60px higher, and rotation widens the footprint, so reserve headroom (the gallery pads 70px above).

examples.title: Nearly settled stamp
examples.code:
import { Stamp } from "@/jbm/ui/stamp"

<Stamp text="REVISADO" press={0.9} angle={-7} />

qa: Drag Press through 0, 0.5, 0.62, 0.8, and 1: hidden, faint while descending, touching down, fully inked, and settled with no jump.
Drag Stamp angle to both extremes: the rotated box stays inside the preview on narrow screens.
Check the offset second impression reads as ink texture, not a duplicate label, and screen readers hear the text once.

items.name: tape-marker
items.title: TapeMarker
items.description: Folded vermilion paper checkpoint marker with an optional label above it.

api.summary: A 20×72 vermilion strip with the shared paper shadow and a darker 14px fold at the top. Usable alone or as PaperTape's checkpoint marker.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional bold vermilion text centered 8px above the marker. It does not wrap and sits outside the marker's box, so reserve headroom for it.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged last onto the marker strip, e.g. for positioning.

stage.basis: Fixed 20×72 box. The label is absolutely positioned above it (8px gap plus one line of inherited-size text) and does not add to the box; long labels extend sideways beyond 20px.

examples.title: Labeled checkpoint
examples.code:
import { TapeMarker } from "@/jbm/ui/tape-marker"

<TapeMarker label="parar aquí" />

qa: Toggle Marker label: the marker box does not move or resize, and the label centers above it.
Check the top fold reads as a darker band and the shadow matches other paper surfaces.
Check long labels at narrow widths: they do not wrap, so make sure they are not clipped by a parent.

items.name: paper-tape
items.title: PaperTape
items.description: Strip of paper fed out by length, with printed marks, checkpoint markers, and attachments on one coordinate system.

api.summary: A card strip with an ink edge and paper shadow that grows from the source as `length` increases. Paired ink dashes are printed every 72 paper px, and markers and attachments ride on the same paper coordinates, so feeding the tape moves them together. Only marks, markers, and attachments inside the visible window render; the viewport clips at its bounds.

props.name: length
props.description: Paper fed out so far, in stage px. Increase it to feed the tape; negative or non-finite values count as 0.

props.name: window
props.description: Visible run in stage px; also the component's width (horizontal) or height (vertical).

props.name: thickness
props.description: Strip thickness in stage px; minimum 16.

props.name: direction
props.description: `horizontal` feeds along x; `vertical` feeds along y and turns markers 90°.

props.name: markers
props.type: { id: string; at: number; label?: string }[]
props.description: Checkpoint TapeMarkers placed at paper coordinate `at` (0 = start of the paper). `id` must be unique within the tape; `label` shows above the marker.

props.name: attachments
props.description: Arbitrary React content pinned at paper coordinate `at`, below the strip (horizontal) or beside it (vertical). IDs must be unique across markers and attachments.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged last onto the outer viewport, e.g. width or overflow.

api.summary: Converts a paper coordinate to its screen distance from the tape's origin; markers, attachments, and printed marks all use it.

params.name: length
params.description: Paper fed out so far, as passed to PaperTape.

params.name: coordinate
params.description: Position on the paper, measured from the start of the paper.

api.returns: Screen offset in stage px: length − coordinate (length clamped to ≥ 0). Values within the window are visible.

stage.basis: Horizontal default: width = window (400), height = thickness + 150 (48 + 150); the strip sits 48px from the top to leave room for markers and labels. direction="vertical" gives width thickness + 180 (228) by height window (400). maxWidth is 100% of the container. Stage orientation does not change the box.

examples.title: Tape with a checkpoint
Feed from a Remotion timeline

qa: Drag Feed from 0 to 1: the strip grows from zero, printed dashes, the marker, and the note move together, and nothing appears before its coordinate is fed out.
Toggle Vertical tape: markers rotate 90° and attachments sit beside the strip; check both directions at narrow widths.
Toggle Checkpoint marker: the tape and note do not move.
Try a very long length: only the visible dashes render and content past the window is clipped at the edge.

items.name: frontmatter
items.title: Frontmatter
items.description: Key/value metadata between literal YAML delimiters, with per-row emphasis, dimming, and a stacked layout.

api.summary: Mono definition list framed by `---` lines on a cream block. Two columns (keys at least 112px, values twice as wide) by default; `stacked` puts each value under its key at full width. Static: no timers or animation; change row props to emphasize or dim fields.

props.name: rows
props.description: Fields in display order. Each row renders `key:` and its value; `key` is also the React key, so keep keys unique.

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stack each value under its key in one full-width column, for narrow or portrait compositions.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged last over the cream background, 18px padding, and 14px mono type; use for width or font size.

api.summary: One field: `key` (string), `value` (ReactNode), optional `highlight` (3px vermilion bar left of the key), and optional `dim` from 0 to 1 (clamped; 1 fades key and value to 28% opacity).

stage.reason: Width fills the container (minWidth 0) and height follows the rows. Chrome adds 36px of padding, two delimiter lines, and 24px of list margin; rows are separated by 12px (6px plus 12px per value when stacked), and long values wrap anywhere. Set style.width for a fixed box.

examples.title: Stacked skill metadata with an emphasized and a dimmed field
examples.code:
import { Frontmatter } from "@/jbm/ui/frontmatter"

<Frontmatter
  stacked
  rows={[
    { key: "name", value: "pdf-processing", highlight: true },
    { key: "description", value: "Extrae tablas de archivos PDF." },
    { key: "license", value: "Apache-2.0", dim: 0.6 },
  ]}
/>

qa: Toggle Stack fields: two-column mode keeps keys aligned at 112px minimum; stacked mode indents values under their keys with no overlap.
Toggle Highlight fields: only the vermilion bar appears; text position does not shift because the bar space is always reserved.
Drag Dim optional field from 0 to 1: key and value fade together to about 28% opacity and stay legible.
Check a long unbroken value on a narrow screen: it wraps inside the block instead of overflowing.

items.name: folder-contents
items.title: FolderContents
items.description: Folder that opens to reveal a sheet and a fan of nested folders whose documents extract independently.

api.summary: Fills Folder's children slot with a front sheet and nested folders, each with an optional document. Every part is a rigid object that translates into view; nothing stretches. Pure React: `open`, per-entry `reveal` and `documentReveal`, and `lift` are independent 0–1 controls with no internal timer. Other SVG props pass through to the Folder svg.

props.name: label
props.description: Mono label on the outer folder's front panel; also names the image for assistive technology. Truncated after 16 characters.

props.name: tone
props.description: Outer folder fill: vermilion accent or ink.

props.name: open
props.description: Outer folder opening from 0 (closed, contents hidden) to 1 (contents shown). Clamped. Defaults to 1 here, unlike Folder's 0; every reveal is multiplied by it.

props.name: entries
props.description: Nested folders, back to front. Their tabs pack between y 24 and 72 of the folder space, so more entries overlap more tightly instead of growing the folder. Empty by default.

props.name: sheet
props.description: Label printed on the front sheet (first 15 characters). An empty string removes the sheet.

props.name: lift
props.description: Raises all contents together by up to 240 folder units (0–1), clipped at the folder's top, for handing the whole group out.

api.summary: One nested folder: `id` (React key), `label` (truncated after 15 characters), `reveal` 0–1 (default 1; rises from the folder bottom), optional `document` label (12 characters shown), and `documentReveal` 0–1 (default 0; lifts the document 45 units out of its folder).

stage.basis: Renders Folder's fixed 260×220 viewBox at 260×220 stage pixels; entry count, reveals, and lift never change the box. Pass width (or style.width) to scale with height auto, and it shrinks to maxWidth 100%. The gallery uses width={320} with overflow visible so the opened sheet above the viewBox stays visible.

examples.title: Open project folder with one extracted document

qa: Drag Open folder through 0, 0.5, and 1: the sheet and nested folders slide up as rigid shapes and never cut through the front panel.
Drag Extract documents and Lift contents independently; each moves only its own objects.
Set Nested folders to 0 and 8: zero entries with an empty sheet reads as an empty folder; eight entries pack tighter without resizing the folder.
Toggle Reveal nested folders: hidden folders sit fully below the rim with complete outlines, clipped only at the container bottom.
Uncertain: at open 1 the sheet and front folders extend above the 220-unit viewBox, so they rely on overflow visible; check clipping when overflow is left hidden.

items.name: folder-carry
items.title: FolderCarry
items.description: Folder carried along a path by its tab, interpolating size and label between two resting places.

api.summary: SVG group (render inside an <svg>) drawing the shared folder silhouette at `carriedFolderGeometry(from, to, path, progress)`, with a fold line and the label fading from the tab to the front panel. Pure React with no timer: drive `progress` from a slider or video timeline, and place a hand at `pointOn(path, progress)`.

props.name: from
props.description: Resting geometry at progress 0, in the parent SVG's units (see tableFolderGeometry).

props.name: to
props.description: Resting geometry at progress 1; may be a different scale or a drawer's own geometry.

props.name: path
props.description: Grip points in the parent SVG's units; start at folderGrip(from) and end at folderGrip(to) so the endpoints do not jump.

props.name: progress
props.description: Carry progress from 0 (at `from`) to 1 (at `to`), by arc length along `path`. Clamped.

props.name: label
props.description: Folder name (first 16 characters); also labels the group as "Carrying …" for assistive technology. Shown on the tab at 0 and on the front panel at 1, crossfading between.

api.summary: Geometry of the carried folder: its grip sits on `pointOn(path, progress)` while width, height, tab size, and tab offset interpolate linearly from `from` to `to`.

params.name: from
params.description: Geometry at progress 0.

params.name: to
params.description: Geometry at progress 1.

params.name: path
params.description: Grip path in SVG units; must have at least one point.

params.name: progress
params.description: 0–1 carry progress; clamped.

api.returns: A FolderGeometry to pass to FolderOutline or to position a hand.

api.summary: Where a hand holds a folder: the tab's horizontal center, 10/27 of the tab height below the top.

params.name: g
params.description: Folder geometry.

api.returns: The grip point in the same units as `g`.

api.summary: Geometry of a Folder-sized silhouette resting at `at`, scaled from Folder's 260-unit frame (body 205×150 at offset 25,55; tab 83 wide, 27 tall, 17 slope).

params.name: at
params.description: Top-left of the 260-unit folder frame, in SVG units.

params.name: width
params.description: Frame width in SVG units; 260 matches a standalone Folder.

api.returns: A FolderGeometry for `from` or `to`.

api.summary: Folder silhouette box: `x`, `y` (top of the tab), `w`, `h`, `tabX`, `tabWidth`, and optional `tabHeight` (27) and `tabSlope` (17), all in SVG units.

stage.reason: Draws in the parent SVG's coordinate space with no box of its own; its extent is set by `from`, `to`, and `path`. The gallery demo uses a 450×270 viewBox at 100% width with folders 100 and 190 units wide.

examples.title: Carry a folder from a small to a large resting place
examples.code:
import { FolderCarry, folderGrip, tableFolderGeometry } from "@/jbm/ui/folder-carry"

const from = tableFolderGeometry({ x: 5, y: 65 }, 100)
const to = tableFolderGeometry({ x: 225, y: 60 }, 190)
const path = [folderGrip(from), { x: 200, y: 45 }, folderGrip(to)]

<svg viewBox="0 0 450 270" width="100%">
  <FolderCarry from={from} to={to} path={path} progress={0.5} label="proyecto" />
</svg>

examples.title: Put a hand on the grip
examples.code:
import { FolderCarry, folderGrip, tableFolderGeometry } from "@/jbm/ui/folder-carry"
import { pointOn } from "@/jbm/lib/geometry"
import { Mano } from "@/jbm/motion/mano" // install @jbm/mano separately

const from = tableFolderGeometry({ x: 5, y: 65 }, 100)
const to = tableFolderGeometry({ x: 225, y: 60 }, 190)
const path = [folderGrip(from), { x: 200, y: 45 }, folderGrip(to)]
const progress = 0.4

<svg viewBox="0 0 450 270" width="100%">
  <FolderCarry from={from} to={to} path={path} progress={progress} label="proyecto" />
  <Mano at={pointOn(path, progress)} pose="pinch" size={70} anchor={{ x: 6, y: 10 }} />
</svg>

qa: Drag Carry progress to 0, 0.5, and 1: the folder matches its resting geometry exactly at both ends, and the label moves from tab to front panel without both copies fully visible mid-way.
Toggle Show hand and sweep progress: the pinch stays on the tab's grip throughout; adjust Hand angle and confirm the contact point does not drift.
Check the scale change reads as smooth growth with no jump in tab shape at the endpoints.
Check narrow screens: the demo SVG scales to 100% width without clipping either resting place.
